title: At the top of a toss, the upward speed is zero
summary: NASA Glenn says that at the highest point of a ballistic toss, the vertical velocity is zero.
body: NASA Glenn's ballistic-flight page says that at the highest point in the flight, the vertical velocity is zero. The sideways speed is a separate part of the motion and is not what this sentence sets to zero. The page treats that peak as a step in the ballistic equations, which ignore drag. A real ball with air drag is described on another Glenn page. This page was last updated 15 July 2024.

sources.title: Ballistic Flight Equations
sources.author: Nancy Hall, NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.note: Public-domain NASA Glenn page, last updated 15 July 2024. Paraphrase of the sentence that vertical velocity is zero at the highest point.
